note: Belgravian Moments longlist (14 Nov 2026): every candidate from the full sweep not chosen for moments.json. status reserve = strong enough to swap in; considered = checked and set aside (see note).

items.modernHeadline: Walkers win all three national road-walking team titles in one season
items.why: Walkers win all three R.W.A. team titles (Junior 10 miles, 20 miles, 50 km) in one season - a first for any club - and hold all five R.W.A. trophies.
items.verified: Editorial states no other club had won all three; Colin Sutton scored in all three; Coleman brothers dead-heated for the Junior title (B81-06).
items.extract: No other club has ever at any time won all three championships; and to do so in the space of three months is almost miraculous.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave Hall in Wimbledon becomes the club's own freehold
items.why: After 25 years of halfpenny schemes, football competitions and collecting "bricks", the club owns Belgrave Hall outright
items.verified: B108-07 (A.A.H.) traces the building fund from the 1920s to the freehold purchase; B108-03 gives the 16 March 1950 announcement. Completion may have been just after; B110-03 marks the purchase; rebuilt hall completed early 1955 (B121-03).
items.extract: These humble beginnings and the application of Belgrave team work at its best over many years has now had its reward and we now own our own headquarters—free from debt, debentures, mortgages and the rest of it.

items.modernHeadline: John Regis wins Olympic relay silver in Seoul
items.why: Olympic medal for a Belgravian: John Regis in the GB 4x100m relay silver at Seoul, in a UK record; Gary Staines also an Olympic 5000m finalist.
items.verified: Short report with heat/semi/final splits: GB (Bunney, Regis, McFarlane, Christie) 2nd in 38.28, 1/10 behind USSR; Staines 13th in the 5000m final. Event day not printed.
items.extract: John Regis strikes relay silver! John, Elliott Bunney, Mike McFarlane and Linford Christie set a new UK record of 38.28 secs to finish 1/10 sec. behind the USSR.

photo.caption: An "unfit" John Regis was persuaded to run a 400m relay leg in the first B.A.L. Match at Birmingham and clocked an impressive 45.36 split - wearing his new "1 piece".

items.modernHeadline: Belchamber places Tommy Green among the greatest walkers
items.why: J. B. Belchamber's long essay ranks Tommy Green among the great walkers since the 1870s professionals: the best piece of writing in the early gazette.
items.verified: 12,900-character essay; table of Brighton stage times. Photo of Green (Daily Sketch) is on the facing editorial B30-03, the first photo of him in the gazette.
items.extract: So is it not true that the select few who stand by right upon the peak of the mountain must close in a little in order to make room for our champion?

photo.caption: T. W. GREEN, whose fine performances on the road have added considerably to Belgrave prestige and given us ample reason to acclaim him as one of the best long-distance walkers ever.

items.modernHeadline: Tommy Green wins the 100 km walk in Milan
items.why: Green wins the international 100 km walk at Milan a year after finishing second there; the gazette prints a translation of the Italian press report.
items.verified: Full translation of Il Mezzogiorno Sportivo; win first announced in B39-03 (Oct-Nov 1930). Issue is Jan 1931, event Nov 1930 (the old shortlist dated it Jan 1931).
items.extract: A phrase such as "Green, incomparabile ed instancabile" scarcely requires translation. and such compliments coming from sportsmen on the Continent make us prouder than ever of "our Tommy."

photo.caption: T. W. GREEN, whose fine performances on the road have added considerably to Belgrave prestige and given us ample reason to acclaim him as one of the best long-distance walkers ever.

items.note: Strong, but three Tommy Green moments already; kept as first reserve.

items.modernHeadline: Footer wins the Southern and Footer and Penny earn England vests
items.why: Three Saturdays in 1933: Bert Footer wins the Southern, the walkers win a record fourth R.W.A. Junior, and Footer and Penny are picked for England after the club's first placing in the National.
items.verified: All three claims are in the text; B58-03 adds Footer 4th and Penny 9th in the International at Caerleon. Footer is also the first holder of the new Club Honours Badge.
items.extract: The three successive Saturdays, February 25th, March 4th and March 11th—brought with them three performances of outstanding merit which focussed the eyes of all the athletic world upon Belgrave and more than ever fortified our right to be considered the greatest all-round athletic club in the country.

photo.caption: "OUR BERT." H. E. FOOTER.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the Southern cross-country title for the first time
items.why: First Southern cross-country title, the step between county success and the 1935 National.
items.verified: Supports the first 'Southern' win at Taplow, 81 pts to Surrey A.C. 97, Penny 2nd; Lord Desborough presented the cup. Previous-shortlist item, confirmed.
items.extract: Firstly, it will be seen that in the period under review, from 1925 until this year, we have improved from 14th to Champions; and that every year, with one exception, the number of points scored has been cut down, until this year we are below the hundred.

items.modernHeadline: The club meets under the shadow of the Munich crisis
items.why: The AGM held at the height of the Munich crisis: the war shadow reaches the club; Bayliss retires as Hon. Sec. after 11 years.
items.verified: Text supports 46 present, small numbers 'due to the crisis', and the 'International situation, then menacing'. Also Harley takes over as Gen. Hon. Sec.
items.extract: The President, W. L. Bayliss, presided, 46 members being present. the smallness in numbers being due to the crisis.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the English Cross-Country title again, at Manchester
items.why: Second English cross-country title, won at Manchester in the last season before the war.
items.verified: Only a stop-press note: supports the win at Manchester and the R.W.A. Junior walk win a week earlier. Fuller report should be in B86 (next slice) - check there for date and detail.
items.extract: As we go to press comes wonderful news of the winning of the English Cross-country Championship at Manchester.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave Hall keeps athletics going in the first winter of the war
items.why: First wartime season: the club keeps racing and its Wimbledon quarters become a hub for athletics in the South
items.verified: Text supports no club championships in wartime, the 20th Open Walk held, quarters lent to Surrey AAA, SCCCA, RWA etc., and lists members in the Forces.
items.extract: Additionally, our quarters have become a focal point of Athletics in the South. Athletes of other Clubs have been invited to come along, and the Surrey County A.A.A., Printing and Allied Trades C.C. Association, South of the Thames C.C.A., Southern Committee of the R.W.A., Southern Counties C.C.A., and "News of the World" S.C., have all been granted the use of our quarters for their promotions.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave remembers members killed in the Second World War
items.why: Wartime losses: young members killed at sea, in Sicily and in North Africa
items.verified: Text records W. H. Bowers (R.N., ship mined), R. V. Reynolds (ambushed in Sicily) and Pat Ridge (Irish Guards, N. Africa, former Army shot and discus record holder). Other losses in B91-29, B92-48, B95-20, B98-56, B99-06.
items.extract: R. V. Reynolds (East Yorks). He was caught in an ambush in Sicily, and to quote his O.C.: "He would have received the M.M., but it is not awarded posthumously."

items.printedHeadline: The Diamond Jubilee Dinner and Dance
items.modernHeadline: Diamond Jubilee dinner marks 60 years of Belgrave Harriers
items.why: The Diamond Jubilee Dinner, 60 years on, where a club doctor publicly took on officials over feeding Britain's Olympic hopefuls
items.verified: Text confirms date and venue (Duke of York's HQ, Chelsea); Dr C. Woodard warned of "near disaster" for 1948 and Jack Crump replied. Jubilee year framed in B102-03.
items.extract: Dr. Woodard said that in his opinion British Athletics faced near disaster in 1948, through lack of proper food and either wrong attention or no attention of athletical injuries, from which so many of our Olympic prospects suffer.

items.modernHeadline: Stan Vickers and Eric Hall walk for Britain at Melbourne
items.why: Two Belgrave walkers, Eric Hall and Stan Vickers, at the Melbourne Olympics, told first-hand
items.verified: Text supports Vickers leading the 20 km and Hall's view he deserved a medal; B128-16 confirms two walkers selected. Vickers' final place not printed here.
items.extract: Perhaps the greatest moment of the Games, for me, was to see two of our men leading an Olympic field - and one of them a Belgravian.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave walkers win all three national team titles in one season
items.why: First club ever to hold all three Senior National road-walking team titles (10 miles, 20 miles, 50 km) in one year
items.verified: B131-33 and editorial B131-03 both state it was never done before; B131-27 counts 20 National Senior walking titles. B131-03 says Preston, B131-33 says Leyland.
items.extract: Our team recorded the best-ever score, one point less than our 1956 record. We completed a trio of Senior Championships in one season - never before accomplished by any club; truly an eventful day !

items.modernHeadline: Stan Vickers out-sprints Ken Matthews to break the 56-year-old two-mile walk record
items.why: Vickers beats Ken Matthews with a 90.4 sec last lap to break George Larner's 1904 two-mile walk record at the White City - one of the great duels of British walking.
items.verified: B143-38 calls the 13:02.4 a "United Kingdom All-Comers Record" and says it broke Larner's long-standing record; B163-54 (1967 retrospective) calls Larner's 13:11.4 a 56-year-old "world record". Use "record" wording carefully.
items.extract: As the back straight was hit Matthews hesitated momentarily. Vickers, like an animal awaiting a mistake by it's prey, seized the initiative with a vicious sprint, and before Matthews had recovered sufficiently to start closing the gap Stan was well on his way to a new United Kingdom All-Comers Record of 13:02:4, 7.2secs ahead of his rival.

items.printedHeadline: IT'S GOLD! AFTER 11 YEARS: NEWS OF THE WORLD SOUTHERN 'BRIGHTON'
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the Southern London-to-Brighton relay for the first time in 11 years
items.why: Belgrave win the News of the World Southern London-Brighton relay for the first time since 1952, with five consecutive fastest stage times.
items.verified: Text supports win by 3 min 10 sec from Portsmouth, 20 teams; date taken from the social column in the same issue, not the report itself.
items.extract: A great day for Belgrave with a win on the Brighton road for the first time since 1952.

photo.caption: THE WINNING LONDON-BRIGHTON RELAY TEAM (Southern Event) ON THE SEA-FRONT WITH THE PRESIDENT AND THE "NEWS OF THE WORLD" TROPHY. REAR:(L.toR.) P. Newell, W.Kerr,Geoff.North,R.Linstead,The President, A.Fairclough,B.Sawyer,C. Dabbs. FRONT:(L.toR.)J.Thresher,Gerald North,L.O'Hara,A. Black. (C.W. Walker was not present).

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave make their first overseas club tour, to Langen in West Germany
items.why: The club's first foreign tour - a return visit to Turnverein Langen near Frankfurt, written up by a woman member; start of a lasting twinning-style friendship.
items.verified: Text explicitly says "This was our first foreign tour". Party included women (Selsonia, Josie Newell) and Tokyo-bound Jim Hogan as a guest. Langen had first visited London 13-16 Aug 1963 (B151-41).
items.extract: This was our first foreign tour -it shouldn't be our last.

photo.caption: The Official Reception Ceremony. (L.to R.) Langen's Vice-President, Bill Lucas, Mrs. Lucas, Burgomaster of Langen, Mrs and Mr Berry of Blackpool and Herr Bernhardt,

items.modernHeadline: Tommy Green, 1932 Olympic walk champion, dies aged 80
items.why: Death of 'Smiling' Tommy Green, 1932 Olympic 50 km champion and arguably the greatest Belgravian; the obituary tells his whole story (gassed in WW1, took up walking to heal his lungs).
items.verified: Percy Wright's obituary supports date, Olympic win (4:50:10, Los Angeles 1932), four London-Brighton wins, six Manchester-Blackpool wins. John Keown's fuller notes in B189-72.
items.extract: His facial features gave the impression that he was smiling even when suffering, and he became known as "Smiling" Tommy. Thousands would line the roadside of the longer distance events just to watch him go by.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the 50th London to Brighton walk, individually and as a team
items.why: At the 50th London to Brighton walk Belgrave supply both the winner (Ray Middleton) and the winning team - their 21st team win on the A23.
items.verified: Gordon Doubleday's report supports the individual win (8:10:21), team win (36 pts v Surrey WC 45) and the count of 21 Belgrave team wins to Surrey WC's 19.
items.extract: So, for the 50th "Brighton" the Bels provided both individual and team winners, Cock of the Walk indeed!

items.printedHeadline: World Best for Belgrave Boys 50 x 1 mile
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave boys run 50 x 1 mile relay to send John Bicourt to the Olympics
items.why: Fifty Belgrave boys run a 50 x 1 mile relay in the rain to fund John Bicourt's Olympic preparation; he went on to run in Montreal.
items.verified: Report (ARM) supports the event, 5:46:39.8 total, £106 profit added to £250 from the club; the 'world best' is self-described ('so far as we know no club has attempted it before'). Bicourt reached Montreal but not the final (editorial B192-06).
items.extract: If John Bicourt does make it to Montreal there will be 50 lads glued to their TV sets this July knowing that they helped put him there, for when the sponsors dues were collected and counted there was a handsome profit of £106 to add to the £250 already donated by the Club.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave women win their first national team medals
items.why: Two years after women were admitted, the Belles win the club's first national team medals in a women's event.
items.verified: Report supports 3rd team (Rook 9th, L. Nicholls 12th, Pritchard 23rd) in the senior 5 km; Shirley Rook missed the coach and drove herself (also B198-107). First Belgrave ladies' national team was 5th in Dec 1977 (B196-23).
items.extract: So, we had won our first set of National Team medals in a Womens' event - the first of many we hope.

items.printedHeadline: XIII COMMONWEALTH GAMES - EDINBURGH - 24 JULY/2 AUGUST 1986
items.modernHeadline: John Gladwin takes Commonwealth 1500m silver behind Steve Cram
items.why: John Gladwin's Commonwealth 1500m silver behind Steve Cram, after he and Regis won AAA titles within two hours of each other (B210-39).
items.verified: Vivid eyewitness report: Gladwin broke 500m out, led until Cram caught him with 160m left; 2nd in 3.52.17. Regis 8th in the 200m final. Medal presented by the Duke of Edinburgh.
items.extract: Just before the home straight he took off. Giving it everything into the bell and round to the backstraight - a 200m he covered in 24.6! - John opened up a gap that was scarcely believable in this class of field.

photo.caption: Following a remarkable season including winning the AAA's 1500m title, second in the Commonwealth 1500m and new club mile record John Gladwin beat a class field including John Walker, Jack Buckner, Tim Hutchins and Dave Moorcroft to win the London Mile in record time.

items.modernHeadline: Centenary cross-country race on Wimbledon Common
items.why: Centenary cross-country match on Wimbledon Common against the ECCU, Surrey and Middlesex - the first big event of centenary year, with the club's surviving England XC internationals present.
items.verified: Supported: snow kept Rotherham away; Bob Treadwell (Surrey) won, Gladwin 7th; 50 runners each got a bone-china centenary tankard; Tom Carter underwrote the cost; Verne Blowfield back at Belgrave Hall for first time in 37 years. Previous-shortlist item - verified.
items.extract: Fifty runners had commemorated our 100 years of existence and each was awarded a Belgrave Centenary bone-china tankard as a memento of the occasion.

photo.caption: On page to Right Top The Start P.Eales(39) and R.Treadwell(43) to the fore for Surrey closely followed by R.Nerurker(21) and S.Fielding(20) for (E.C.C.U) and Belgravians J.Wright(18),J.Gladwin(10), J.Chaston(5),G.Tiernan(16),F.Ward(17) and M.Chaston(6).

items.note: Covered by the centenary birthday moment (B212-16).

items.printedHeadline: EVENT ROUND UP OF INDIVIDUAL PERFORMANCES
items.modernHeadline: John Regis wins World Championships 200m bronze in a UK record
items.why: Regis takes World Championships 200m bronze in a UK record in centenary year - the club's individual highlight of 1987; Marcus Adam also European Junior 200m champion.
items.verified: Event round-up quotes Ron Pickering's TV commentary and Regis's own words; text says he 'collected the Bronze medal in a new UK record'. Long item - extract is Regis's quote.
items.extract: I couldn't have predicted that I'd get in the top three but in saying that I've trained hard, worked hard with my coach, come back from injury and now I'm in effect the third best in the World at this moment.

photo.caption: MUSCLE BOYS :: "JUNIOR" ATHLETES MARCUS ADAM And PHIL GOEDLUCK SHOW THAT THEY HAVE ARM AS WELL AS LEG POWER - WATCH OUT KEN ONUAGULUCHI..

items.printedHeadline: McVitie's Gold Challenge 25 x 1 Mile Relay.
items.modernHeadline: Gary Staines runs a solo sub-four-minute mile at Battersea Park
items.why: Gary Staines runs a solo sub-four-minute mile in the 25 x 1 mile relay - billed as the world's first.
items.verified: Reprint of an APA press release: 3:59 on the final stage, unopposed, at Battersea Park (B212-40 confirms the race moved there from Crystal Palace); 'world's first' is the press release's claim.
items.extract: THE WORLD'S FIRST SOLO SUB-FOUR MINUTE MILE IS ACHIEVED IN McVITIE'S CHALLENGE

photo.caption: Gary Staines finishing the final stage of the 25 x 1 mile Relay.

items.modernHeadline: Sue Morrison becomes the club's first woman secretary
items.why: The club's first woman Honorary Secretary in its 100 years.
items.verified: Profile by Eric Crutcher states plainly it is a first; she joined in early 1986 via the ladies' walking section. Exact appointment date not given.
items.extract: For the first time in the club's illustrious history we have a lady secretary.

photo.caption: Bill Lucas presents the Open 7 Miles Walk winning team awards to our Ladies - Gill Brackpool, Jill Borthwick and Sue Morrison.

items.modernHeadline: The club mourns President Bob Ricketts, founder of its walking section
items.why: Tribute to President R. W. 'Bob' Ricketts, who kept the club alive when it was down to four active members and founded its walking section.
items.verified: Says the walking section began as a section he formed at Erith in the war, and credits him with the National title; the R. W. Ricketts Shield and Doris Shield are his gifts (B19-04).
items.extract: Not many years ago a small room in Floor Street, Chelsea, was the meeting place of four members who at that time represented the active section of the Harriers. Bob had little support to encourage him, but he stuck to his job rather than take the easy course of joining another Club.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the National road walking team title at Leicester
items.why: Belgrave win the R.W.A. National 20 miles team title for the third time (138 starters), with McMullen 4th.
items.verified: Team 33 pts to Sheffield United 53. Not the first title: Belgrave also won in 1924 and 1925 (and 1929 for a fourth in five years, B26-06), so the moment is better framed as the 1924-29 run.
items.extract: Five of our Club stalwarts, in three thrilling and exciting hours, won a title which gives distinction to the Club name wherever athletes are gathered.
items.note: Real (12 May 1928, Leicester) but the club's third National walking title, not the first (first was 1924, per B34-08).

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave walkers march at Nijmegen with England's team
items.why: Belgrave walkers, Tommy Green among them, go abroad with the first English team at the Nijmegen Four Days marches.
items.verified: Written by L.E.F.; names Green in the 40-man English team. The walks were opened to all countries that year after walking was dropped from the 1928 Olympics. Nijmegen later gave its name to the R.W.A. team shield Belgrave won in 1933 (B19-11, B58-03).
items.extract: On paper it looks quite easy for trained long-distance walkers to do thirty-four miles a day for four days in succession, with a daily time limit of eleven hours. It would be unwise, however, to talk of such easiness to any of the forty men who comprised the English team; for it is difficult to imagine a more gruelling affair than the marches of 17th to 20th July, 1928.

items.modernHeadline: The gazette prints its first photograph: President Harry Hare
items.why: First photograph printed in The Belgravian: President W. H. Hare, founder-editor of the gazette.
items.verified: No item before B20 has a photo. Caption lists Hare's offices and his National (1924-5) and Junior (1922) team wins. AGM report also records 109 new members in the year.
items.extract: It gives me great pleasure to state that the Club is stronger than ever. Since the last A.G.M. we have enrolled 109 new members, against which we have had 25 resignations

photo.caption:
OUR PRESIDENT—W. H. HARE, Esq.
Club Hon Sec., 1921-2-3-4.
Club President, 1927-8.
President, South of Thames Cross Country Association, 1928.
Member of winning Belgrave teams National Road Walking Championship, 1924-5 and Junior Road Walking Championship, 1922.
Club 20 miles Champion, 1923.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the South of the Thames cross-country title for the first time
items.why: First South of the Thames senior cross-country team title, at Gatton Park, Merstham, plus the Dewar Shield and Colman Cup.
items.verified: Text: 'out first victory' (sic), 89 points, previous best 3rd in 1904 and 1928; Footer missed it through illness.
items.extract: The triumph of our team in the 32nd race for the South of the Thames Cross-Country Association's Championship at Gatton Park, Merstham, marks a very definite step in the recent rapid improvement of our Cross-country Section.

items.modernHeadline: Bert Footer is the first Belgravian to win the South of the Thames
items.why: Bert Footer becomes the first Belgrave runner to win the South of the Thames individual title.
items.verified: Text says 'He is the first Belgrave runner to win this championship'; photo credited to The Daily Telegraph. Footer went on to win the Southern in 1933 (B57-03).
items.extract: He is the first Belgrave runner to win this championship and so gains for himself a unique position in our Club history.

photo.caption: "OUR BERT." H. E. FOOTER.

items.modernHeadline: How Belgrave became National walking champions, 1922-1929
items.why: The club's own history of the R.W.A. National: first title at Windsor in 1924, then 1925 (by one point at Derby), 1928 and 1929.
items.verified: Gives team members and placings for each year; confirms 1926 race cancelled by the Coal Dispute (General Strike, B7-06). The 1925 win is reported first-hand in B3-12.
items.extract: Windsor Park was the venue of the next race, and here we made our debut as National Champions.

items.modernHeadline: Harry Hare's halfpenny plan for a club house
items.why: W. H. Hare's halfpenny scheme launches the Belgrave Building Fund, the club's first serious push for a clubhouse of its own.
items.verified: Hare says he has kept every halfpenny for three years (1,080 coins) and costs a £2,000 clubhouse; B56-21 reports a house in Lauriston Road, Wimbledon considered and dropped at about £2,500.
items.extract: Has anyone realised the insignificance and yet the power of the humble halfpenny, or as it is more commonly termed, "a'penny"?

items.modernHeadline: Tommy Green picked for the Los Angeles Olympics
items.why: Tommy Green is selected for Los Angeles, 'the first Belgrave man to attain Olympic honours'.
items.verified: Text supports selection and hopes for gold 'before the end of August'; Hampson (second-claim) is also wished luck. Better used as the lead-in to B54-04 than as its own moment.
items.extract: To Tommy Green has befallen the honour of being the first Belgrave man to attain Olympic honours

items.modernHeadline: 'Four Famous Walkers': Green in his Olympic vest
items.why: Full-page photo of four Belgrave walkers, Green in his Olympic vest, reproduced from the Birmingham press.
items.verified: Caption names Bidgood, Green, Rickards and Bentley. It is the sixth photo in the gazette (after Hare 1928, Gordon 1929, Green 1929, Footer 1930, Belchamber 1931) and the first group photo.
items.extract: J. C. Bidgood, T. W. Green (in Olympic vest), F. Rickards and F. E. Bentley.

photo.caption: J. C. Bidgood, T. W. Green (in Olympic vest), F. Rickards and F. E. Bentley. "Four Famous Walkers." This was the title given to this photograph when it appeared in the Birmingham Sunday Mercury.

items.modernHeadline: Bill Rice dies, aged 31, on Brighton Relay day
items.why: Death of Bill Rice, Track Captain and Social Hon. Secretary, aged 31, on the day the club won its third Brighton Relay; the W. A. Rice Memorial Trophy followed.
items.verified: Supports death on 25 April aged 31 after long illness; B82-03 records the W. A. Rice Memorial Trophy for the Junior 880 yards. B73-04 records another young member dying the same day.
items.extract: Even as life ebbed, in his delirious thoughts he lived again his races on the Club's behalf; and, on April 25th, as the Brighton Relay (in which he had captained previous victorious teams) drew to a close, so did our beloved friend's life, at the early age of 31 years.

items.modernHeadline: Jim Ginty runs the steeplechase at the Berlin Olympics
items.why: Jim Ginty selected for the Berlin Olympic steeplechase; the club also fights the R.W.A. over Fred Bentley's omission from the walk team.
items.verified: Supports Ginty's selection and the Bentley protest; B75-04 reports Ginty went out in his heat and members travelled to Berlin. B84-23 calls Ginty 'Belgrave's only representative in 1936'.
items.extract: Now it gives us all the greatest of pleasure to congratulate Jim upon his inclusion in the British Olympic team.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave's cross-country team appears on television
items.why: Belgrave's Paris-winning team is televised from Alexandra Palace in the BBC's first months of TV - an early TV appearance for the club.
items.verified: Supports the broadcast from Alexandra Palace with Bert Footer addressing viewers, and the Baird-process note. A quirky first rather than a sporting landmark.
items.extract: On Wednesday, January 27th, the winning Surrey County team, and our victorious team which competed in Paris, were televised from Alexandra Palace.

items.modernHeadline: Paris club visits Wimbledon for the first international race at home
items.why: First visit of a foreign club to race Belgrave at home: the Paris Metro club U.S.M. run at Wimbledon.
items.verified: Supports 'the first visit of a foreign club'; B83-03 adds the Mayor of Wimbledon officiated; B80-16 has the French club's own article. Belgrave won with six in the first eight.
items.extract: This year, however, marked a very special occasion, none other than the first visit of a foreign club to compete against our boys on their own soil.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave look ahead to the 1940 Olympics that never happened
items.why: A hopeful survey of Belgrave's candidates for the 1940 Helsinki Olympics, written months before war cancelled them - captures the club on the eve of war.
items.verified: Text is a forward-looking selection survey (Churcher, Bentley, Penny, Footer etc.) and mentions Stampfl's winter training. Poignancy depends on outside knowledge that the Games never happened.
items.extract: The next Olympiad is due to be held in Finland next year, and those athletes who entertain hopes of inclusion in the British team are already planning their training.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win a relay interrupted by an air raid warning
items.why: A relay won during the Blitz summer, restarted after an air raid warning
items.verified: Text confirms Belgrave won by nearly 4 minutes; Charlie Smart ran on after the race was held up by an air raid warning.
items.extract: Charlie Smart, who continued after the restart through an air raid warning, in which the race was held up, to increase the lead, which was carried on by Tom Carter and Len Herbert, who finally broke the tape nearly 4 mins. ahead of the 2nd team.

items.modernHeadline: Racing through the flying-bomb summer of 1944
items.why: The "Flying Bomb Number": racing on through the V-1 summer with scratch teams and bombed-out members
items.verified: Text supports fixtures with Polytechnic Harriers cancelled or run with scratch teams, members' homes damaged or destroyed, no serious injuries reported.
items.extract: This edition might well be called the "Flying Bomb Number," as much of what is recorded took place whilst Southern England, and particularly London, was under attack by these missiles.

items.modernHeadline: Derrick Burfitt wins the first National Youths' cross-country
items.why: Derrick Burfitt wins the first National Youths' cross-country race, in the last winter of the war
items.verified: Text supports Burfitt winning by ~250 yards in 16:58.2 at West Bromwich; only three Belgrave youths turned up so no team.
items.extract: From the fall of the starting flag the race was dominated by our own Burfitt. At the end of the first lap he was comfortably ahead by some 90 yards and the farther he went the greater the lead he gained.

items.printedHeadline: Seen at Wembley during the Olympic Games.
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave officials help run the 1948 Olympics
items.why: Belgrave officials everywhere at the 1948 Wembley Olympics
items.verified: Previous shortlist item: verified; light-hearted list of members as starters, judges, announcer and stewards. Best paired with B104-04.
items.extract: Yes, Belgrave were well in evidence—on the track competing for the honour of Britain, in the crowd witnessing unforgetable sport and performances—and wherever wanted, giving a hand with the big and little jobs which go to make up the tremendous organisation of the World's largest sports meeting.

items.modernHeadline: Wartime member Etienne Gailly takes Olympic marathon bronze at Wembley
items.why: Etienne Gailly, a Belgian paratrooper elected a Belgrave member in wartime (1944), collapses in the lead in the 1948 Olympic marathon and staggers home for bronze.
items.verified: Feature (1999) supports: 'On April 29th 1944 Etienne ... was elected a member of Belgrave Harriers'; result 3. Gailly 2:35:33.6. Caveat: club decided he would not count as a Belgrave 'international' as he lived in Belgium. Previous-shortlist item; the event belongs to 1948.
items.extract: On April 29th 1944 Etienne (immediately becoming known as Steve) was elected a member of Belgrave Harriers

photo.caption: A shattered Etienne Gailly is led away from the finish of the Olympic Marathon of 1948.

items.note: Used as the photo for the 1948 Olympics moment (B104-04).

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave sprinters win their first AAA relay title
items.why: First AAA team title for the sprinters, a sign of the new all-round club
items.verified: Text confirms first AAA relay win, 4 x 110 yds in 42.6s ("second fastest time by a British Team"): Merrett, Holtum, Walden, Mayers. Year from issue (Nov 1954).
items.extract: with 50 yards to go I saw Ivan's face break into a grin and I knew that it was ours.

items.modernHeadline: Coach Franz Stampfl leaves Belgrave for Australia
items.why: Farewell to Franz Stampfl, the club's professional coach since 1937, leaving to coach Australia
items.verified: Text supports he joined in summer 1937, returned c.1951 as professional coach, credited with the strongest-ever sprint team; leaving for Adelaide University and to be National Coach of Australia.
items.extract: Franz came to Belgrave as a young man in the summer of 1937 and quickly endeared himself to those with whom he came in contact. Within a few weeks he had organised our training as it had never been done before. He did not ask us to do what he himself could not. His enthusiasm and personality were such that members were attempting to do things they had previously avoided.

items.modernHeadline: First inter-club floodlit meeting held at Tooting Bec
items.why: The first inter-club floodlit meeting at Tooting Bec, for the Melbourne Trophy
items.verified: Text says "the first inter-club Floodlit Meeting" — a first for the venue/competition, not necessarily the first floodlit athletics anywhere.
items.extract: On a cold damp evening at Tooting Bec, the first inter-club "Floodlit Meeting" was held for the "Melbourne Trophy".

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave's Ranjit Bhatia runs for India at the Rome Olympics
items.why: Ranjit Bhatia, Oxford student and Belgrave road-relay star, runs for India at the Rome Olympics after Belgrave officials help secure his selection.
items.verified: Text supports birth in London, Oxford scholarship, club 5¾ record, Bob Taylor/Les Cohen contacting the Indian Olympic Committee, and his Rome heat. Elected Vice-President 1960.
items.extract: At 24 years of age Ranjit had gained the highest award attainable by an athlete-that of representing his country at an Olympic Games.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave launch their own road relay and beat Portsmouth by 14 seconds
items.why: Belgrave stage their own invitation 12-stage relay for Southern clubs to fill the gap left by the end of the Southern London-Brighton - and win it.
items.verified: Text supports first promotion, 21 teams, win by 14 sec over Portsmouth, organised by Bill Lucas. B158-04 editorial (Mar 1966) records News of the World withdrawing from all road relays.
items.extract: The race was promoted by Belgrave to fill the gap left by the cessation of the Southern London - Brighton road relay

photo.caption: Trevor Hart hands over to Charlie Walker with Weatherill (Portsmouth) waiting to take over from the fast-finishing Tulloh.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the North Surrey Cross-Country League for the first time
items.why: First North Surrey League title (forerunner of today's Surrey League) at the fourth attempt, won on depth: 23 different scorers.
items.verified: Text supports title after runner-up finishes in 1963-65; Belgrave went on to win four in a row (B169-72). Same-issue items also record the first Surrey senior XC title since 1952 (B158-50, B158-07).
items.extract: So, after the fourth attempt, we have at last won the League title. Belgrave had 23 different runners filling the ten scoring positions in the four fixtures---a reassuring thought when one considers that each combination was good enough to give us a win in 3 races out of 4, and a second place in the other.

photo.caption: CENTRE: A confident team await the start. (L to R): Black,Merry,Geoff North Gerry North,Dear,Steer,Major and Dabbs.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave walkers win three of the four national team titles
items.why: Golden age of club walking without star internationals: three of four National senior road titles in 1968-69, plus London-Brighton, after the club's first National 20 km title in 1968.
items.verified: Text supports 3 of 4 National titles (20 km, 20 miles, 50 km) and London-Brighton (17th win). B166-61 records the first R.W.A. 20 km team title (Coventry, 11 May 1968) as the club's 32nd R.W.A. team win.
items.extract: During the R.W.A. year 1968-69 (September '68 to August '69) Belgrave Harriers' Walking Section equalled, if not surpassed, the achievements of the great club teams of 1957 and 1960

items.modernHeadline: Tommy Green starts the 50th Belgrave Open Seven walk
items.why: The 50th Belgrave Open 7 walk, started by 1932 Olympic champion Tommy Green, with Mrs Savage who had made tea at the first one still there.
items.verified: Text supports 50th edition, Tommy Green starting, ~150 walkers, Belgrave team win by 84 points, Mexican guests.
items.extract: 50 open 7's is quite some record for a promoting club so that it was only right that the 50th should be started by Tommy Green who took the Gold Medal for the 50 Kilometres Walk in the 1932 Olympics .

photo.caption: A corner of Belgrave Hall showing the heaving mass of steaming bodies that go to make up an Open '7'.

items.printedHeadline: Sept 15th - EUROPEAN POSTMANS WALK CHAMPIONSHIP - LONDON
items.modernHeadline: Ray Middleton wins the European postmen's walk in full uniform
items.why: Ray Middleton, 'Belgrave's walking postman', wins a European title at Crystal Palace in full postal uniform, in front of Blue Peter.
items.verified: Short report supports the win over 15 km in 1:13:03 against some 40 uniformed postmen from six countries.
items.extract: Carrying his 34 years and a full postal uniform with deceptive ease Ray Middleton showed the world's press and Blue Peter just how versatile a walker he is by easily winning the European Post Office Walking Championship.

items.modernHeadline: Laurie O'Hara wins the world veterans' 5,000m title in Cologne
items.why: Laurie O'Hara becomes world veterans' 5,000 m champion at the first big international veterans' meeting - start of a long veterans era for the club.
items.verified: Report supports O'Hara winning the 5,000 m final, with Clive Shippen 5th and 2nd in the steeplechase. Cover of the same issue shows O'Hara on the rostrum. He later won world vets gold again at Hanover 1979 (B199-93).
items.extract: Showing his usual flair and a speedy finish, Laurie O'Hara demolished the field in the 5,000 metres final at the World Veteran's meeting in Cologne.

photo.caption: Front Cover. Laurie O'Hara on the winners rostrum after the 5,000m final at the International Veterans Meeting at Cologne

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave's first trophy, the 1897 Haig Cup, returns to the club
items.why: Belgrave's first ever trophy, the 1897 Haig & Haig Cup, won outright by Sam Sherrington in the club's early years and kept on a family sideboard, comes home 72 years later.
items.verified: Clive Shippen's history supports the 1897 gift by G.O. Haig, outright win by Sam Sherrington, return by his son Lionel in 1974 and re-presentation at the 88th dinner; Haig then sponsored the 12-stage relay. Text says Sherrington's third win came 'by 1920' but also 'after only six years' - internal inconsistency on the year.
items.extract: It was on that evening that Belgrave's first ever trophy, the HAIG & HAIG CHALLENGE CUP, reappeared in public and, in addition a renewed association was made with the whisky company itself, now John Haig & Company Limited.

photo.caption: On behalf of Michael Henderson, Managing Director of Haig & Haig, David Couzens presents the Haig Cup to his father and President of Belgrave Harriers, Bill Couzens.

items.modernHeadline: Death of Ed Lacey, sports photographer and Belgrave member
items.why: Tribute to Ed Lacey, the world-famous athletics photographer (Beamon's leap, Bedford v Puttemans) who was a Belgrave member and supplied hundreds of the gazette's photos.
items.verified: Obituary supports membership from February 1948, freelance career from mid-60s, Tokyo 1964 breakthrough. Many earlier Belgravian photos are credited to him (e.g. B175-02).
items.extract: Ever eager to oblige, a phone call to him from the Editor saying,"One of our chaps is competing in the big meeting this weekend," would invariably result in a sheaf of full plate photo's arriving on Monday morning.

items.printedHeadline: NATIONAL WIN - For Carl and Team.
items.modernHeadline: Carl Lawton wins the national 20km walk and Belgrave take the team title
items.why: Carl Lawton wins his first national title and leads Belgrave to the R.W.A. 20 km team title, joining the club's line of national champions.
items.verified: Doubleday's report supports Lawton 1st in 92.25 and Belgrave team 1st (42 pts v Sheffield 53); 14 disqualified, 21 retired of 137.
items.extract: Yes, its congratulations from all Belgravians upon winning a National R.W.A. Championship, thus taking yourself alongside Tommy Green, Harry Churcher, Stan Vickers, Eric Hall, Ray Middleton and Wilf Wesch.

items.modernHeadline: 33 Belgravians run the first London Marathon
items.why: 33 Belgravians finish the first London Marathon - the running-boom era arrives.
items.verified: Supported: 33 members finished, 'most of whom were our older brethran'; Laurie O'Hara first Bel in 2:37.53; Pam Davis among finishers. Light, period-flavoured report.
items.extract: Belgrave ran and finished 33 members most of whom were our older brethran.

items.modernHeadline: Walker Dave King killed during the London to Brighton race
items.why: Tragedy on the Brighton Road: Dave King, holder of a record 8 London-Brighton team medals, fatally injured in a car accident during the race.
items.verified: Jack Goswell's tribute: King lying 14th when hit, three days before his 39th birthday; career detail from 1962. B201-25 records his 8th winning team medal ('world record'). No private details.
items.extract: "ALAS" out of victory came "TRAGEDY" to leave us all in the depths of despair at the finish, to learn the news of a serious car accident involving one of the 'Clubs Stalwarts' of the Brighton Road, 'David King' when lying fourteenth in the race, his injuries being so serious they proved fatal.

items.modernHeadline: Ernest Obeng beats Olympic champion Allan Wells over 100m
items.why: Sprinter Ernest Obeng, 'the fastest Belgravian of all times', beats Olympic 100m champion Allan Wells at Crystal Palace.
items.verified: Supported by this farewell item, the T&F review (B203-49) and the cover photo (B203-01). Obeng (Ghana) was then returning home after a Reading University Masters; he stayed a member and came back to win AAA indoor titles.
items.extract: Athletically this has been his finest year with a long series of International Competitions in which he was always well placed, his efforts being flashed across our T.V. screens and culminating in that fine Coca Cola meeting win over Olympic 100m Champion Alan Wells on a balmy September evening.

photo.caption: At last! Ernest Obeng's look of joy records his Coca Cola meeting victory in the 100m over Olympic Champion Alan Wells.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the Wellington International Relay in Ostend
items.why: Belgrave win the Wellington International Relay at Ostend - only the second British winners in 28 years; the club's first overseas team win of the era.
items.verified: Supported; 12-leg medley on Ostend racecourse, Gladwin took the lead on the 1200m 6th stage. Editorial B207b-04 confirms 'only the second winning British team in the 28 years of the event'. First visit was 27 March 1983 (B206-67, 6th).
items.extract: And so we were all pleased -not because the winning time was exactly 1 minute faster than last years- but because our men ran for each other and were impressive as a Team!

photo.caption: Our victorious team after their outstanding win in the Wellington Relays held on the race course at Ostend.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave reach Division 1 of the British League
items.why: Five seasons after entering at Division 5, Belgrave compete in Division 1 of the British Athletics League in centenary year, finishing 4th.
items.verified: Match-by-match report: first top-flight match at Portsmouth (6th), Gladwin towing Coe to a league 800m record; B212-27 confirms 4th in Division 1. Rise Div.5 (1983) to Div.2 confirmed by B209-138; first BAL match win B207-42 (7 May 1983, Warley).
items.extract: On a beautiful sunny day, Belgrave began their first year in Division 1 of the British Athletic League.

photo.caption: TEAM SPIRIT

items.modernHeadline: Belgravians win four golds at the Auckland Commonwealth Games
items.why: Belgrave athletes win 4 gold, 2 silver and a bronze at the 1990 Commonwealth Games in Auckland, including Marcus Adam (200m) and Andrew Lloyd (5000m).
items.verified: Text: 'The Belgrave medal and points haul had risen to 4 Gold, 2 Silver, 1 Bronze'. Golds per B214-50: Adam 200m, Lloyd 5000m, Adam and Regis in England 4x100m. Mainly a manager's travelogue. Previous-shortlist item.
items.extract: The Belgrave medal and points haul had risen to 4 Gold, 2 Silver, 1 Bronze, 3 fourths and a sixth.

photo.caption: BACK COVER: Commonwealth Champion at 200m,Marcus Adam sits this one out at a Division 1 British League meet.

items.printedHeadline: Women's Surrey CC League Division 1 Race 4, Reigate Priory, 19 Feb
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave women win the Surrey Cross Country League in their first top-flight season
items.why: Belgrave's women win the Surrey Cross Country League Division One in their first season in the top division - the women's section's first big team title.
items.verified: Text: 'Belgrave were declared overall winners of division one ... a historic victory', Gabby Collison individual winner. B220-42 records promotion from Division 2 in 1992/93 and the first Surrey Women's Summer Road League win in 1992; B221-58 says 1993/94 was 'their very first season in Division One'.
items.extract: Eventually Belgrave were declared overall winners of division one with match positions of 2nd, 2nd, 1st and 2nd - a historic victory.

photo.caption: Above: At Reigate for the last of the 1993/94 Womens"Surrey League races Morag Andrew (25) heads the main pack which includes Martina Ryan (27) and Helen Maskrey (26) but it was Helen who was first home for the Belles in 5th place.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the London Marathon team title
items.why: Belgrave win the London Marathon team title, with Paul Evans third overall and Gary Staines ninth.
items.verified: Results: 'Teams: 1, Belgrave 9:56:02; 2, Morpeth'; text calls it 'the classiest Club Championship of all time'. Previous-shortlist item.
items.extract: This race must go down as the classiest Club Championship of all time.

photo.caption: Below right: Paul Evans earned selection for the Olympic Marathon after yet another top class run, but will he take up the offer?

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the Surrey cross-country title for the first time in 30 years
items.why: Belgrave regain the Surrey county cross-country team title after 30 years - a return to the club's harrier roots, followed in 2000 by the first Surrey League title in 28 years.
items.verified: Text: 'we have to go back 30 years for our previous victory when our outstanding runner of that day was Gerry North'. Related: B228-93 (Surrey League title, 5 Feb 2000, 'first time in 28 years'), B226-73 (best South of Thames win since 1895, 14 Feb 1998).
items.extract: Whatever success we gain in Track & Field and however you measure the prowess of an athletic club, we know that underlying it all we started as a Harrier club - and it hurts when we are no longer seen as one.

photo.caption: A cold-ridden Roger Alsop (8) was unable to hold back the ever improving Dave Beaver (12) at Happy Valley

items.printedHeadline: Back home again! The Millennium Arena, Battersea Park
items.modernHeadline: Battersea Park track reopens as the Millennium Arena
items.why: Belgrave's historic home track at Battersea Park, used since 1921, reopens as the £2.6m Millennium Arena.
items.verified: Text supports the reopening and gives the club's history on the site from 27 Dec 1921; old track closed May 1999. B227-09 reports the lottery grant approval.
items.extract: It seems possible that we first used a track in Battersea Park as long ago as 27th December 1921 for the traditional Boxing Day handicaps.

photo.caption: The assembled dignitaries of Wandsworth Council join Belgravians, Track Staff, Surrey representatives and Tessa Sanderson on official opening day - 1st June 2000.

items.printedHeadline: Beijing - so near yet so far
items.modernHeadline: Idowu takes Olympic silver and Sayers sets a British record in Beijing
items.why: Phillips Idowu wins Olympic triple jump silver and Goldie Sayers sets a British javelin record in fourth at Beijing 2008.
items.verified: Text supports both: Idowu silver behind Evora (17.62 v 17.67); Sayers 4th, 38cm off bronze, with British record 65.75m. Related golds: Idowu Commonwealth (B241-02, 2006), European Indoor (B254-02, 2007).
items.extract: And while Goldie was in that cruellest position, just out of the medals, Phillips was in and out of the lead twice in the triple jump, finishing up disconsolate with the silver medal.

items.modernHeadline: An early member remembers the club around 1888
items.why: Rare first-hand memory of the club in its first years: 'Up the Bels' round the bridges, pub club rooms, and a failed 1890 clubhouse plan.
items.verified: Tom Jones's letter in Feb 1928 issue; dates are from memory ('about').
items.extract: One night about 40 years ago I first heard the old battle cry of "Up the Bels." whilst running "Round the Bridges,"

items.modernHeadline: Club history uncovers 1908 Olympic sculling champion H.T. Blackstaffe as a Belgrave president
items.why: Club research reveals that Belgrave's 1909-12 President H.T. Blackstaffe was an Olympic gold medallist (1908 single sculls) - rewriting the belief that Tommy Green was the club's only Olympic champion.
items.verified: Text supports it; caveat: his gold was in rowing for Vesta RC, not athletics, and the text says his joining date is unknown as early minute books are missing.
items.extract: It has always been accepted that the great long distance walker, Tommy Green, was our first, and to date, only, Olympic gold medallist when he triumphed in the 50 kilometre event back in 1932 in Los Angeles. While Tommy, without a shadow of a doubt, was the first athlete from the Club to win the highest award in our sport we had a man who won a gold medal back in 1908 and was our President from 1909 to 1912 - H.T. Blackstaffe.

photo.caption: Photo from Vesta Rowing Club's collection

items.modernHeadline: A fighter plane crashes beside the Doris Shield meeting
items.why: Vivid period piece: a burning fighter plane crashes beside the Richmond track during the Doris Shield meeting.
items.verified: Pilot parachuted onto a Mortlake roof unhurt; athletes ran to the wreck. Belgrave kept the Doris Shield.
items.extract: Several athletes put up unofficial mile records running to the burning plane, and the rest of us had to be reminded that this was an athletic meeting before the Two Miles Walk could be started.

items.printedHeadline: THE H. T. BLACKSTAFFE SHIELD RACE.
items.modernHeadline: The Blackstaffe Shield: a trophy from an Olympic champion
items.why: History of the club's oldest championship trophy, given by H. T. Blackstaffe, 1908 Olympic sculling champion and club President in 1909.
items.verified: The roll printed here covers only 1920-1928 (top three); the full roll from 1910 is in the first issue (B2-07). Footer wins the 1929 race. Better as background than a timeline moment.
items.extract: Until 1909, however, there existed no trophy for the event, and then Mr. H. T Blackstaffe, the Olympic Sculling Champion of 1908, and President of our Club in 1909, presented the Shield that bears his name. This was competed for on January 22nd, 1910, for the first time, from "The Spencer Arms," Lower Richmond Road, Barnes Common, then the Club headquarters, and won by C F. Blow

items.modernHeadline: Walkers keep the national 50 km team title
items.why: Walkers retain the R.W.A. 50 km team title and Horlick Cup (first won 23 June 1934, B65-10; won a third time at Derby in 1936, B74-06).
items.verified: Previous-shortlist item, confirmed: team of Green (2nd), Bentley (6th), Rickards (7th) won by one point over Birmingham W.C.; the rest of the editorial is Building Fund and HQ notes. Better as part of a 50 km run than alone; the first title (B65-10) is the stronger date.
items.extract: Congratulations to the team which made the long journey to Bradford and successfully defended our title of National Champions in the 50 kilometres Walk, held on Whit Monday.

items.printedHeadline: A FLIGHT OF FANCY INTO THE FUTURE.
items.modernHeadline: A wartime vision of Belgrave in 1960
items.why: Vivid wartime dream of the club's post-war future, written while members were scattered
items.verified: A fantasy, not an event; useful as era colour or reserve.
items.extract: I am sitting in one of the offices devoted to the production of "The Belgravian," lavishly illustrated these days and published weekly, and recognised as the leading authority on all matters concerning Athletics.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the first Surrey road relay
items.why: First winners of the new Surrey County road relay
items.verified: Previous shortlist item: verified, Belgrave won 1:30:27 and became first holders of the Underhill Trophy. County-level; low priority.
items.extract: We thus became the first holders of the "Underhill" Trophy awarded to the winning team

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the Chelmsford Road Relay for the first time
items.why: First Chelmsford Road Relay win, seen as a pointer to the 1951 National
items.verified: Previous shortlist item: verified; first win of the Sidney Taylor Cup. Minor on its own.
items.extract: Belgrave put up a fine performance to win the trophy for the first time by a good margin from the holders, Aylesford Paper Mills S.C.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave come back to win the Southern Road Relay
items.why: Comeback win in the Southern Road Relay with course records on five stages
items.verified: Text supports Belgrave winning 3.48.34, 5 seconds outside the 1938 record, after trailing Essex Beagles by 2.5 minutes; Jack Brown, Bruce, Tooby, Adams set course records. Previous shortlist item: verified, a good race but secondary to the 1951 National.
items.extract: Len Adams had other ideas and, running like a man possessed, he not only beat the course record by a second, but he gained 1 min. 28 secs. on the leaders and we still had a fighting chance.

items.modernHeadline: The Belgravian publishes its 150th issue
items.why: The Belgravian reaches its 150th issue with a potted history of the gazette: first photo 1929, wartime editions as the link to members in the Forces.
items.verified: Text supports W.H. Hare first editor 1925, first photograph Sept/Oct 1929, wartime editors called up one after another, 40-page issue No.100.
items.extract: Despite great difficulties and war- time austerity, two issues were provided for each of the war years.

items.printedHeadline: GREAT WIN BY GERRY ! ..... but BELS fail to topple POMPEY
items.modernHeadline: Gerry North wins the Southern cross-country title
items.why: Reserve: Gerry North wins the Southern cross-country title by a huge margin - the era's top Belgrave distance runner.
items.verified: Text supports the individual win (team 2nd to Portsmouth) and the footnote that his GB top and car were stolen afterwards.
items.extract: "His best ever", "outstanding", "scintillating", "devastating", "a great champion". These were just a few of the superlatives heard at Parliament Hill when Gerry North won his first Southern Counties C.C.Championship

photo.caption: LEFT: Gerry North storms round the final circuit with a minute's lead.

items.modernHeadline: Alf Harley becomes first Belgravian president of the Southern Counties AAA
items.why: Alf Harley - "Mr Belgrave", editor of 59 issues and Hon. Secretary for 30 years - becomes the first Belgravian President of the Southern Counties AAA.
items.verified: Text supports first Belgravian SCAAA President, member since 1926, 59 editions edited, 30th anniversary as Hon. Sec. in Sept 1968. Headline is EDITORIAL.
items.extract: A.A.Harley is the first Belgravian to hold this prestigious office and all will agree that "Mr Belgrave", as he is sometimes called, is the fitting person for such a "first".

items.printedHeadline: Silver in National Relay - FINE TEAMWORK BY BELS
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave take silver in the National 12-stage road relay
items.why: Best placing yet in the new AAA National 12-stage relay: silver behind Coventry Godiva.
items.verified: Text supports 2nd in 4:07:02 behind Coventry 4:05:01, Tipton third; "probably the best 12 man team we have ever turned out". Previous-shortlist item - genuine but secondary to B152-20.
items.extract: We fielded our strongest possible team for this event - in fact it was probably the best 12 man team we have ever turned out and hopes of a win ran high

photo.caption: A perfect 'change-over' and John Bicourt sets off to continue the good work done by our fastest man of the day - Geoff North.

items.modernHeadline: Carl Lawton is first Briton behind Mexico's Olympic champions in the Jubilee 20km walk
items.why: Previous-shortlist item: Carl Lawton is first Briton (6th) behind five Mexicans led by Olympic champion Daniel Bautista in the Queen's Silver Jubilee 20 km, winning the Southern title.
items.verified: Text supports Lawton 6th in 92:44 and Southern champion, Belgrave open and Southern team wins. A good race, but no Belgrave victory over the stars; better as context for Lawton's 1979 national win (B199-60) than as a timeline moment.
items.extract: Over the next lap (less than two miles) Bautista and Colin "changed gear" and opened up a gap, we were now seeing world class walking.

photo.caption: Mexicans filled the first five places in the Southern Jubilee 20km, the winner being Olympic Champion Daniel Bautista (115). Carl Lawton (6) was the first Briton home in sixth place.

items.note: Lawton 6th, first Briton behind the Mexicans: good background, not a club landmark.

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave veterans set a 25 x 1 mile relay best
items.why: Belgrave veterans, average age 47, set a 25 x 1 mile veterans' best by over 12 minutes inside the 100 x 1 mile relay.
items.verified: Bill Laws's report supports 2:17:38, 12:32 inside Sale Harriers' 1977 time; 'World Best' is the club's headline claim.
items.extract: The average time for the 25 stages was 5 min. 30.3 while the average age of the team turned out to be no less than 47 years.

photo.caption: Belgrave's triumphant record breaking 25 x 1 mile vets team. (Well almost all of them) - We're not certain how John Walker got in the photo!

items.modernHeadline: Belgrave youths win the Surrey cross-country title
items.why: Belgrave youths sweep the Surrey title (team 15 pts) with Dave North beating John Gladwin - the first glimpse of the generation that drove the 1980s revival.
items.verified: Previous-shortlist item, verified: North 1st, Gladwin 3rd, team won the newly presented Hathway Shield; 4 Bels in Surrey Youths Inter-Counties team. The heading's 'record' is not explained in the text. Club-level result - fine as reserve, not a top moment.
items.extract: At 3 miles all seemed lost for Dave as the leaders stretched into the final hilly mile but suddenly as the spectators crowding around the finishing lane waited it was Dave North first in sight some 10 seconds clear - a truly inspired surge.

photo.caption: Belgrave's Youths Team in the Surrey C.C.Championships. L.to R. Dave North, Gerry Sexton, Mark Waller, John Gladwin and Alister Horton.

items.note: A Surrey youths title; the "record" is never explained.

items.modernHeadline: Rebuilt Belgrave Hall and new gym officially opened
items.why: Belgrave Hall, the clubhouse bought in the 1930s, reopens rebuilt with a new gym - opened by the AAA Secretary.
items.verified: Supported: opened by Mike Farrell; GLC grant of £14,000 rescued the project; Hall now used ~70 hours a week. Completion detail in B208-19 (club room, gym run by Mike Winch and Judy Oakes).
items.extract: Past Presidents travelled from all over the UK to see the conclusion of a project that many had helped start with the purchase of the Hall way back in the 1930's.

items.printedHeadline: SOUTHERN COUNTIES AA 12 STAGE CHAMPIONSHIPS COMBINED WITH THE BELGRAVE HARRIERS 12 STAGE RELAY - WIMBLEDON
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win the Southern 12-stage road relay
items.why: Belgrave win the Southern Counties 12-stage road relay, held with their own Belgrave relay on its silver jubilee - an early sign of the relay revival.
items.verified: Text: '1990 was a corker with Bels winning to celebrate the silver jubilee of our popular relay'; 1989's 6th was 'our best result for nearly 20 years'. Mostly a results table. Previous-shortlist item; moderate strength.
items.extract: While 1989's 6th place was our best result for nearly 20 years 1990 was a corker with Bels winning to celebrate the silver jubilee of our popular relay.

photo.caption:
1990 Southern 12-Stage Relay

Justin Chaston anchors the Belgrave winning team. Later in the year he transferred to Texas where no doubt he wore Union Jack shorts!

items.modernHeadline: Micky Pyer becomes the first member to reach 70 years with the club
items.why: Micky Pyer becomes the first Belgravian to complete 70 years of unbroken membership - a living link to the 1920s teams.
items.verified: Text supports it; he joined 1921, club mile champion 1922-23, 3rd scorer in the 1928 National. Includes a 1926 photo. Obituary B222-21 (died 1994).
items.extract: On the 21st October 1991 MICKY PYER became the first ever Belgravian to reach 70 years of unbroken membership.

photo.caption:
Micky Pyer (extreme left) lines up at the start of the Belgrave 10 mile C.C. Championship in 1926. Having won the title in 1923 and 1924, this time he had to give way to his captain Bert Footer.

items.printedHeadline: Avrupa Sampion Kulüpler Kupasi Atletizm — 22nd European Champion Club's Cup
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave finish third at the European Champion Clubs Cup in Istanbul
items.why: Belgrave place third at the European Champion Clubs Cup in Istanbul - the best British club result on continental soil.
items.verified: Text: club record 3:09.30 4x400m 'ensured third place overall and the best ever British performance in the European Clubs' Cup on Continental soil'. Previous-shortlist item; date of meeting not given.
items.extract: A superb new Club Record of 3:09.30 which ensured third place overall and the best ever British performance in the European Clubs' Cup on Continental soil.

photo.caption: Below: Belgrave's fastest ever 4x400 metres squad - Jon Ridgeon, Tom Lerwill, David Nolan and Chris Rawlinson

items.printedHeadline: They've done it again! National 12-Stage title retained
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave retain the National 12-stage road relay title
items.why: Belgrave retain the National 12-stage title - the first club in a decade to defend it.
items.verified: Text: 'the first time in a decade that a club had returned to Sutton Park to successfully defend their title'. Best told as part of the 2002 story (B230-21). Previous-shortlist item.
items.extract: It was the first time in a decade that a club had returned to Sutton Park to successfully defend their title

items.printedHeadline: WB-J is double European Youth Champion
items.modernHeadline: Wade Bennett-Jackson wins double sprint gold at the European Youth Olympics
items.why: Wade Bennett-Jackson, aged 16, wins 100m and 200m gold at the European Youth Olympic Festival in Paris.
items.verified: Text supports both golds (10.70 and 21.38, championship best). Promising youth success rather than a club landmark. Previous-shortlist item.
items.extract: On the last day of the Games, yet another championship best fell to our young Belgravian as he clocked 21.38 for his second gold medal

photo.caption: Above: Young sprint star Wade Bennett-Jackson in indoor action at the National Indoor Arena, Birmingham, back in January 2003.

items.modernHeadline: The Belgravian moves from print to an electronic newsletter
items.why: The Belgravian, printed since 1925, becomes an electronic newsletter (absorbing eHarrier) - the end of the printed gazette.
items.verified: Editorial supports it: committee decision to let eHarrier 'metamorphose into The Belgravian - produced and distributed electronically'. Related: B214-04 (1991) records the earlier two-year gap after Joe Coleman's death.
items.extract: The Belgrave Committee has therefore taken the decision to allow the newsletter eHarrier to metamorphose into The Belgravian – produced and distributed electronically.

items.modernHeadline: Roll of R. Murphy Shield walk champions
items.why: Previous shortlist item: roll of R. Murphy Shield winners 1916-1927.
items.verified: Not a landmark. It is a walking-notes preview in the January 1928 issue (not 1927) with a table of past winners; the same roll up to 1924 was already printed in the first issue (B2-10). The 1928 race is reported in B14-16. Recommend dropping from the timeline.
items.extract: The closest finishes were in 1925 and 1926, when on each occasion, E. L. Reeve was two seconds behind the winner after walking neck-and-neck all the way.
items.note: Not a 1927 moment: a walking-notes preview in the Jan 1928 issue; the same roll (to 1924) is in No. 1. Drop.

items.printedHeadline: " News of The World " Road Relay Race
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave second in a wartime road relay full of service teams
items.why: Wartime road relay with service teams in the field
items.verified: Previous shortlist item: verified; Belgrave were 2nd to Mitcham by 5 seconds, a mis-marked course; not a win. Colour (Canadian Army team) but weak as a moment; B87-16 is stronger.
items.extract: A Canadian Army team had the honour of being the first Service side to finish, and their abbreviated shorts were a sight for sore eyes!

items.modernHeadline: Bill Lucas remembers running behind Wooderson's record three miles
items.why: Bill Lucas, Belgrave's 1948 Olympian, recalls three great crowd moments: Wooderson's 1946 3 miles, Zatopek's 1948 5,000 m, and announcing Ibbotson's 1957 mile record.
items.verified: Vivid writing, but not a 1960s club event; the moments are national ones (Lucas ran in the 1946 race and the 1948 Games). Previous-shortlist item - better used as a quote for the 1948 Olympics entry than as its own moment.
items.extract: Such was the cheering that for the second half of the race it was impossible to hear either the sound of the runners feet on the track or even one's own breathing---it was literally one long continuous roar and I am sure that this must have spurred Wooderson to his great achievement.

photo.caption: BILL LUCAS WINS SURREY '6' OF 1951

items.note: Vivid memories, but of national events (1946-57), not club history.

items.printedHeadline: Bronze in National Relay DERBY SNATCH SILVER
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave win bronze in the National 12-stage road relay
items.why: First National 12-stage relay medal (bronze), lost silver to Derby by 11 sec after a 4¼-hour duel.
items.verified: Text supports 3rd, 11 sec behind Derby, Coventry winning. Previous-shortlist item - verified, but superseded by the 1969 silver (B170-14); keep as related rather than its own moment.
items.extract: So, after 4¼ hours of running, the two teams finished only 11 seconds apart.

photo.caption: The 10th change-over on Leicester's 'K' track, and Adrian Major sends off Gerry North in hot pursuit of Bullivant.

items.printedHeadline: Bronze medals were truly worth the struggle in National 12-stage
items.modernHeadline: Belgrave take National 12-stage bronze, a seventh straight year of medals
items.why: Bronze in the National 12-stage - medals for a seventh consecutive year.
items.verified: Text: 'we still medalled - for a seventh consecutive year'. A good season, not a landmark on its own. Previous-shortlist item; rate low.
items.extract: A trace of early disappointment gave way to the feeling that we had fought well and, let’s face it, although things didn’t go our way we still medalled – for a seventh consecutive year.
